existing.description: The Western Australian Premier's University Scholarship is a Western Australian Government award that provides high-achieving international students with $50,000 towards their course fees and other university costs at one of Western Australia's five universities. Ten recipients are selected annually, with two awarded at each university. Applicants must be new offshore international students, citizens of one of 22 listed countries, and must apply directly to their chosen university, which assesses applications and selects the recipients. The Semester 2, 2026 round closed at 3:00pm AWST on 29 May 2026 and the Semester 1, 2027 round has not yet opened.
eligibility: Be a new offshore enrolment into an undergraduate or postgraduate course at one of Western Australia's five universities

Be a citizen of one of the listed eligible countries: Bangladesh, Bhutan, Brazil, China, Colombia, Hong Kong, India, Indonesia, Japan, Kenya, Malaysia, Nepal, Oman, Republic of Korea (South Korea), Saudi Arabia, Singapore, Sri Lanka, the Philippines, the United Arab Emirates, the United Kingdom or Vietnam
Meet the eligibility criteria published in the application form on the chosen university's website
Not be a domestic student or an onshore international student
existing.eligibility_summary: New offshore international students enrolling in an undergraduate or postgraduate course at one of Western Australia's five universities, who are citizens of one of 22 listed countries, meet the eligibility criteria published by their chosen university, and apply directly to that university.
benefits: $50,000 scholarship towards course fees and other university costs
coverage: $50,000 towards course fees and other university costs, applied against the recipient's fee and tuition account at the enrolling university
requirements: Choose one of Western Australia's five universities and apply directly through that university's official website
Meet the eligibility criteria published by the chosen university
Submit the university application within that university's scholarship window, which opens with the round
documents: Academic records, as assessed by the chosen university
Responses to qualitative questions contained in the university's application
Supporting documents specified by the chosen university
existing.english_requirement: No Government-level English requirement is published; eligibility criteria including English language requirements are set by the chosen university on its application page.
application_method: Choose a participating Western Australian university
Wait for that university to publish its scholarship application page when the round opens
Apply through the university's online application process, which may include academic records, qualitative questions and supporting documents
The university assesses and selects successful students and informs the Department
existing.selection_notes: Applicants are assessed by the selected university on a range of factors including demonstration of a high level of academic achievement as determined by the admitting university; individual universities may require additional qualitative assessment through written or interview responses to short-listed applicants. This is a competitive process.
existing.best_fit: High-achieving new offshore international students from the 22 listed countries enrolling full-time at Curtin University, Edith Cowan University, Murdoch University, the University of Notre Dame Australia (Fremantle) or the University of Western Australia.
existing.notes: Ten scholarships are awarded each year, two to each of the five universities. Applicants must be prepared to decline other scholarships previously granted by the University, State or Commonwealth if those scholarships prohibit holding multiple scholarships, and must not be a recipient of another Western Australian Government scholarship. Payments are exclusive of GST and the University decides the frequency and value of credit towards course fees.
existing.duration: One year of funding, credited against the recipient's fee and tuition account after the University census date for the semester applied for
existing.application_period: Semester-based rounds. Round 7 (Semester 2, 2026 enrolments) ran 9:00am 3 March to 3:00pm 29 May 2026; Round 8 for Semester 1, 2027 enrolments is not yet open.
existing.deadline_display: Applications for Semester 2, 2026 closed at 3:00 PM (AWST) on Friday, 29 May 2026. The Department asks applicants to "check back soon for updates on when applications for Semester 1, 2027 will open"; no Semester 1, 2027 dates are published yet.
existing.program_type: State government scholarship, administered by the participating universities

existing.description: The Vice-Chancellor's International High Achievers Scholarship is a Charles Darwin University award for international students with a record of academic excellence. CDU publishes that it covers 50% of the tuition fee for an undergraduate or postgraduate coursework degree, for the full duration of the course, and that it is neither transferable for cash nor refundable and cannot be transferred to another person, semester, course or year. Applicants must have a minimum overall score of 95% in their highest completed qualification, must be paying international student fees, and must not hold another scholarship from an Australian or foreign sponsoring agency. Results are announced during Orientation Week.
eligibility: Applicant must apply to commence study in Semester 1 or Semester 2 2027, in the intake they are first offered.
Applicant must meet the University's academic and English language entry requirements for their chosen course.
Applicant must have a minimum overall score of 95% in their highest completed qualification.
Applicant must be an international student paying international student fees.
Applicant must not hold another scholarship from an Australian or foreign sponsoring agency.
Applicants must be able to pay their portion of the tuition fees on or before the payment due date, which CDU states is the first day of teaching of each semester.
The scholarship applies to an undergraduate or postgraduate coursework degree.
existing.eligibility_summary: Applicants must be international students paying international student fees who apply to commence study in Semester 1 or Semester 2 2027, meet CDU's academic and English language entry requirements for their course, hold a minimum overall score of 95% in their highest completed qualification, and not hold another scholarship from an Australian or foreign sponsoring agency.
benefits: Results are announced during Orientation Week, earlier than the start of teaching.

CDU's international student scholarships page also lists automatic, no-application-required awards that can sit alongside a study offer, including the CDU Global Merit Scholarship (30% of the tuition fee for select courses, for new international TAFE, undergraduate, postgraduate coursework and higher degree by research students commencing in 2026 and 2027, automatically assessed after submitting a course application) and the CDU Bachelor of Nursing Scholarship (up to 20% of the tuition fee for the Bachelor of Nursing, for new international students commencing in 2027, automatically assessed).
coverage: 50% of the tuition fee for an undergraduate or postgraduate coursework degree, for the full duration of the course.
requirements: Step 1: apply to study at CDU.
Step 2: submit your application for the VCIHAS.
The application form requires an application intake, an Application Number (StudyLink or SATAC) and an email address that matches the one provided in the Studylink application.
The form requires an average overall score in your highest completed qualification, expressed as a percentage.

The applicant statement is mandatory and answers why you should be selected, how you will become an outstanding ambassador of CDU, your extracurricular activities with a focus on community engagement, work experience, creative arts and sport, and how you will use your CDU qualification to make a difference in your community.

A declaration must be ticked confirming the information is true and correct, that you have read and understood the conditions of application, that the decision of the University selection panel is final, that you cannot hold more than one tuition fee scholarship from CDU at a time, that you do not hold another scholarship from an Australian or foreign sponsorship agency, and that you accept you may be asked to provide a student story or testimonial as a scholarship recipient.
The form must be signed and dated.

Ongoing eligibility: continue to be an international student liable for international student fees, pay your portion of tuition fees on or before the first day of teaching of each semester, maintain satisfactory academic progress each semester with a minimum GPA of 5.3 and no fail grade in any unit, and maintain a full-time enrolment of 40 credit points (0.5 EFTSL) each semester unless you have approval to reduce your study load or take a leave of absence for the semester.
documents: Email address as provided in the Studylink application.
Average overall score in your highest completed qualification, given as a percentage.
Applicant statement answering the four published questions on selection, ambassador role, extracurricular and community engagement activities, and community impact of the qualification.
The scholarship page states the supporting statement is up to 600 words; the application form states a short statement of 500 words or less. Confirm the applicable limit with CDU before submitting.
existing.english_requirement: CDU requires all higher education applicants to satisfy the English Language Proficiency Requirements for their chosen course and to supply evidence of this at the time of application. CDU's published minimum English test scores are: IELTS Academic overall minimum 6.5 with no band below 6.0 for postgraduate and overall minimum 6.0 with no band below 6.0 for undergraduate; PTE Academic overall minimum 58 with no score below 50 for postgraduate and overall minimum 50 with no score below 50 for undergraduate; TOEFL overall minimum 79 with a minimum writing score of 21 for postgraduate and overall minimum 60 with a minimum writing score of 21 for undergraduate; Cambridge English Advanced overall minimum 176 with no skill below 169 for postgraduate and overall minimum 169 with no skill below 169 for undergraduate; CDU ELICOS EAP004 for postgraduate and EAP003 for undergraduate; and an approved English test completed within two years of commencement. IELTS One Skill Retake is accepted, allowing a single skill to be retaken within 60 days. Alternative evidence routes published on the same page include Year 12 in an approved English-speaking country, 0.5 FTE of higher education study in an approved country completed within the past five years where relevant, an enabling course, a TAFE qualification at Certificate III or higher, current AHPRA registration, two years of full-time equivalent employment in English-medium roles within the last five years in a recognised English-speaking country, or a primary language pathway declaration.
application_method: Apply to study at CDU and obtain an Application Number (StudyLink or SATAC).
Use the same email address in the scholarship form as in your Studylink application.

Complete the Vice-Chancellor's High Achievers Scholarship (VCIHAS) Application form on CDU's website, including your intended intake, your average overall score as a percentage, and the four applicant statement questions.
Tick the declaration, sign the form and enter the date.
Submit the form before the closing date for your intake: 31 January 2027 for Semester 1 2027 or 4 July 2027 for Semester 2 2027.
Await the outcome; CDU states results will be announced during Orientation Week.
existing.selection_notes: CDU publishes the selection criteria as the overall score in your highest completed qualification plus a supporting statement. The application form adds that the decision of the University selection panel is final, and the declaration confirms the process is competitive. CDU publishes no interview requirement, no weighting for the two criteria, no offer round structure and no appeal process for VCIHAS; other CDU International College scholarships on the same page do publish an interview requirement, so confirm whether an interview applies to VCIHAS.
existing.best_fit: International applicants with a 95% or higher overall score in their highest completed qualification who are applying to commence study at CDU in Semester 1 or Semester 2 2027 in an undergraduate or postgraduate coursework degree and who can fund the remaining 50% of their tuition fees themselves.
existing.notes: This is not full funding: it covers 50% of the tuition fee only, and the recipient must pay their portion of tuition on or before the first day of teaching of each semester. The scholarship is neither transferable for cash nor refundable, and cannot be transferred to another person, semester, course or year. It is conditional rather than open-ended: it ends at the earliest of course completion, exhaustion of the maximum scholarship value, or loss of ongoing eligibility, and retaining it requires a minimum GPA of 5.3 with no fail grade in any unit and a full-time enrolment of 40 credit points (0.5 EFTSL) each semester unless a reduced load or leave of absence is approved. Only one CDU tuition fee scholarship may be held at a time, and holding another scholarship from an Australian or foreign sponsoring agency disqualifies the applicant. No deferral, return-home, clinical restriction, tax treatment or award renewal terms are published on the pages read. Official pages disagree on the statement length: the scholarship page says up to 600 words, the application form says 500 words or less.
existing.duration: The minimum time in which the course can be completed, or until the maximum scholarship value is exhausted, the course is completed, or the recipient no longer meets the ongoing eligibility of the scholarship.
existing.application_period: Applications are open at the time of checking on 1 October 2026. CDU publishes closing dates of 31 January 2027 for Semester 1 2027 and 4 July 2027 for Semester 2 2027, but does not publish a separate opening date for the scholarship.
existing.deadline_display: Applications close 31 January 2027 for Semester 1, 2027 intake, and 4 July 2027 for Semester 2, 2027 intake.
